in_arabic.name: عثمان
in_arabic.meaning: عثمان بن عفان، ثالث الخلفاء الراشدين، زوجة النبي

in_english.name: Uthman
in_english.meaning: Derived from Arabic, meaning 'strong believer, steadfast'
in_english.long_meaning: The name Uthman originates from Arabic roots, specifically from the word 'athm' which means 'to be steadfast' or 'to be strong'. Uthman bin Affan, the third Caliph of Islam and son-in-law of Prophet Muhammad, was a renowned companion and leader known for his piety, generosity, and just governance. The name Uthman symbolizes strength in faith, resilience, and devotion to Islamic principles.

data.cultural_impact: The name Uthman holds an significant place in Islamic history. Uthman ibn Affan (r.a) was the third caliph (successor to the Prophet Muhammad) of the Rashidun Caliphate. During his tenure, the Quran was compiled in its final form. He played a crucial role in the preservation of the Quran as we know it today. He was also a companion of the Prophet Muhammad and contributed immensely to the spread of Islam. Uthman's legacy extends beyond his role as a caliph, as he was also a renowned scholar, orator, and administrator - these qualities have influenced the naming of many Muslim children with the name Uthman.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Uthman holds a spiritual significance for Muslims. Uthman ibn Affan (r.a) was known for his strong faith, wisdom, and pious character. He was one of the Twelve Imamsaab (Companions of the Prophet Muhammad who were granted special grace) and the first to be given the title Taalert Surur, which translates to "the ideal slave of Allah". Uthman's unwavering dedication to Islam and his contributions to the preservation of the Quran make this name a powerful reminder of the importance of knowledge, faith, and devotion to Allah. The name Uthman is a source of inspiration for Muslims today, reminding them to embody the virtues of intelligence, faith, and service to Allah.
